result.title: Invariance before structure: two modes of emergent compression in representation learning
result.comment: Extended abstract, UniReps workshop at NeurIPS 2026
result.summary: Learned representations show striking invariance across biological and artificial neural networks, with different substrates and variations driven by drift, heterogeneity and initialisation. To understand this invariance, we propose Emergent Adaptive Representation Learning (EARL), a framework that distinguishes two modes of emergence in learned representations: state-space compression, where a learned representation gains predictive power over its own future beyond what the network's units can predict individually, and parameter-space compression, where networks with different micro-level parameters converge to the same representation. We formalise both as Fisher sensitivities and introduce ensemble-level information-theoretic measures for each. In a recurrent reservoir with a trained bottleneck, parameter-space compression rises within the first few epochs of training and partly independently of the task, whereas state-space compression rises about 30 epochs later and only when the network begins to learn the temporal structure of the task. These results suggest that invariance to the substrate and task-specific emergent structure are acquired in distinct phases of learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 EARL 框架，区分表征学习中两种涌现压缩：状态空间压缩（表征对自身未来状态的预测力超出单个单元）与参数空间压缩（不同参数的网络收敛到同一表征），并用 Fisher 敏感度和集成层面的信息论指标度量；在一个带训练瓶颈的循环 reservoir 中发现前者比后者晚约 30 个 epoch 出现，且仅在任务时序结构被学到时上升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其区分「跨种子不变」与「状态可预测性」的度量，可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正承载任务必要的时序/结构信息、而非仅由训练动力学决定的稳定偏置提供工具；但实验规模小且非视觉任务，迁移性需人工核查。
